notes: SR88 Oliver Bonas Home. Same access route as bs88 (default-curl-UA SSR fetch + Claude-in-Chrome for JS-hydrated counts; robots.txt blocks /search so relied on nav/footer/sitemap.xml). Sitemap and footer expose a full 'Sale' taxonomy under /sale: 'Sale Homeware' (homeware-scoped) plus sibling non-homeware buckets (Sale Fashion/Jewellery/Accessories/Gifts/Beauty categories) and a separate cross-department 'Last Chance Sale'. The homeware-specific listing is https://www.oliverbonas.com/sale/category/homeware ('Sale Homeware', breadcrumb 'All Sale > Sale Homeware'). No 'See all N items'/'N styles' count renders anywhere for this URL (neither in SSR HTML nor after full JS hydration in a live browser - this template genuinely omits the usual count badge, confirmed by re-fetching 3x and re-checking after full page load/scroll with identical result each time). Recovered the exact count from the site's own Klevu analytics beacon fired by the page itself (network request to stats.ksearchnet.com/analytics/categoryProductViewTracking, klevu_categoryName='Sale Homeware', klevu_categoryPath='All Sale;Sale Homeware'), which enumerates klevu_productIds = 77 distinct product ids; cross-checked against the Filters modal's own Product-Type facet counts, which sum to ~76 (2+1+2+1+2+3+20+2+12+4+2+1+5+1+5+4+6+1+2), matching within 1 (consistent with a single item missing a Product Type tag e.g. an 'Internal Ads' style entry). Also checked whether this same Klevu-beacon method could be silently truncating counts: on two OTHER category pages (Last Chance Sale and a New-In seasonal edit) the beacon returned exactly 100 both times despite the Filters modal proving one of them has >150 real items - strong evidence of a 100-id cap on the beacon. Sale Homeware's 77 is below that suspected cap and is corroborated by the independent facet-sum, so it is trusted as accurate (not truncated). SALE VS CLEARANCE JUDGEMENT: this page is titled/breadcrumbed 'Sale Homeware' (not 'Clearance'/'Outlet'/'Final Sale'/'End of Line'), and its own meta description is generic ('Shop our homeware sale for online discounts, save on home accessories now!') with no explicit permanent-markdown / outlet / end-of-line language on the page. The site DOES have a more strongly clearance-worded concept, 'Last Chance Sale' (https://www.oliverbonas.com/sale/category/last-remaining, breadcrumb 'All Sale > Last Chance Sale') - opened and checked via Filters-modal Department facet: Home (9) Fashion (68) Jewellery (35) Accessories (44) Gift (6) Furniture (5) Small Furniture (2) - i.e. it is a sitewide cross-department clearance bucket with only 9 of ~169 department-tagged items belonging to Home, and selecting the Home facet did not produce a separate bookmarkable homeware-only URL. Excluded from rows per the same 'no isolable homeware-only sub-URL' rule used elsewhere in this pass, but flagging it here in notes since an orchestrator with a wider (sitewide, not homeware-only) scope may want to reconsider it. Sale Homeware itself has genuine visible sub-navigation (Sale Home Accessories, Sale Dining, Sale Lighting, Sale Home Textiles, Sale Mirrors - all real 200-status URLs under /sale/category/homeware/*, verified not to be redirects/facet re-cuts) plus non-homeware siblings (Sale Furniture, Sale Gifts, Sale Beauty) and non-category price-tier filters (Sale Under £10/£20/£30/£50). These sub-URLs are exhaustive subsets of the already-fully-counted 77 (they are the same 'Sale Homeware' Magento category sliced by Product Type), so they were not broken into separate rows to avoid double-counting/padding; only the single comprehensive parent row is reported below, per this project's 'drop mixed/redundant slices, keep the complete listing' convention.
